figures.note: 原论文 Figure 1:四种提示方式在同一任务上的完整轨迹对比——Standard 直答、CoT 只想不做、Act-only 只做不想、ReAct 边想边做。绿色对勾/红色叉号即成败判定。
figures.caption: Figure 1: (1) Comparison of 4 prompting methods, (a) Standard , (b) Chain-of-thought ( CoT , Reason Only), (c) Act -only, and (d) ReAct (Reason+Act), solving a HotpotQA ( Yang et al. 2018 ) question. (2) Comparison of (a) Act -only and (b) ReAct prompting to solve an AlfWorld ( Shridhar et al. 2020b ) game. In both domains, we omit in-context examples in the prompt, and only show task solving trajectories generated by the model (Act, Thought) and the environment (Obs).
figures.captionEn: Comparison of 4 prompting methods: (a) Standard, (b) CoT, (c) Act-only, (d) ReAct, on HotpotQA and AlfWorld.
figures.sourceLabel: Yao et al., ReAct, arXiv:2210.03629, Figure 1

figures.note: 原论文 Figure 1:著名的 U 型曲线——关键信息放开头或结尾效果最好,埋在上下文正中间性能跌到谷底。CH.04「关键内容放头尾」的直接证据。
figures.caption: Figure 1: Changing the location of relevant information (in this case, the position of the passage that answers an input question) within the language model’s input context results in a U-shaped performance curve—models are better at using relevant information that occurs at the very beginning (primacy bias) or end of its input context (recency bias), and performance degrades significantly when models must access and use information located in the middle of its input context.
figures.captionEn: U-shaped performance curve as a function of document position.
figures.sourceLabel: Liu et al., Lost in the Middle, arXiv:2307.03172, Figure 1

figures.note: 原论文 Figure 1:Toolformer 如何自监督地决定「在哪里插入哪个 API 调用」——工具使用的开山思路。
figures.caption: Figure 1: Exemplary predictions of Toolformer. The model autonomously decides to call different APIs (from top to bottom: a question answering system, a calculator, a machine translation system, and a Wikipedia search engine) to obtain information that is useful for completing a piece of text.
figures.captionEn: Toolformer: self-supervised sampling of API calls worth inserting into text.
figures.sourceLabel: Schick et al., Toolformer, arXiv:2302.04761, Figure 1

figures.note: 原论文:Generative Agents 小镇场景——25 个 agent 的记忆/反思/规划驱动拟真社会行为。
figures.caption: Figure 1. Generative agents are believable simulacra of human behavior for interactive applications. In this work, we demonstrate generative agents by populating a sandbox environment, reminiscent of The Sims, with twenty-five agents. Users can observe and intervene as agents plan their days, share news, form relationships, and coordinate group activities. A screenshot of the game world populated by generative agents.
figures.captionEn: Generative Agents: interactive simulacra of human behavior in a small town.
figures.sourceLabel: Park et al., Generative Agents, arXiv:2304.03442
